title: Export business (goods)
tagline: Selling Indian products abroad — B2B buyers, Amazon Global Selling, Etsy, or your own international store.
who: Manufacturers and artisans looking for foreign buyers

structure.recommended: Private limited or LLP (proprietorship works for e-commerce exports)
structure.why: Buyers, banks (packing credit, LCs) and ECGC prefer an incorporated entity; FTP incentive accounts and RCMC are per entity. Small e-commerce exporters shipping by courier can start as proprietors and convert later.
structure.alternatives: Proprietorship for courier-mode e-commerce exports; partnership for family trading houses.

breakdown: Audit + ROC + GST refunds handling: ₹35,000–80,000 a year

timeline: Entity + GST + IEC + LUT + AD code in 3–5 weeks; first shipment as soon as a buyer pays an advance.
taxes: Exports are zero-rated: ship under LUT without IGST and claim refund of input GST (ITC) — 90% is now sanctioned provisionally by the system from Nov 2026 reforms — or pay IGST and claim it back.
RoDTEP scrips (0.5–4.3% of FOB by HS code) and duty drawback on imported inputs; Advance Authorisation/EPCG for duty-free inputs and machinery.
Export proceeds must be realised within the RBI period (9 months after the 22 Sep 2026 amendment; verify) and matched to e-BRCs.
Income tax as per entity; no special export tax holiday outside SEZs.
selling: B2B: buyer databases via EPCs, FIEO fairs, IndiaMART export leads, Alibaba Gold Supplier, LinkedIn outreach, Indian embassies’ commercial wings
B2C cross-border: Amazon Global Selling, Etsy (handmade, GI products), eBay, Walmart Marketplace, Shopify Markets with DHL/FedEx/ShipGlobal
Government: Dak Ghar Niryat Kendras for postal exports; E-Commerce Export Hubs being piloted
sourcing: Clusters: Moradabad brass, Jaipur jewellery and textiles, Tirupur knits, Panipat home textiles, Bhadohi carpets, Agra footwear, Kutch and Lucknow crafts, Kerala spices, Darjeeling/Assam tea, Kashmir/Himachal apples and saffron
APEDA/Spices Board/Tea Board registrations for agri products; phytosanitary and FSSAI export certificates
GI tags add buyer trust abroad
pitfalls: Not ticking RoDTEP/drawback on the shipping bill — the incentive is lost permanently for that shipment.
Letting buyers pay late beyond the realisation window without an AD-bank extension.
Quoting CIF without insurance and freight quotes — freight has swung 300% in recent years.
Ignoring destination rules: EU CBAM reporting, US FDA prior notice for food, CE/UKCA marks, REACH for chemicals, Amazon’s own compliance documents.
Mixing export and domestic stock without separate invoice series — GST refund scrutiny.
